# Tech Radar

A simple, configurable Technology Radar for communicating an organisation's technology strategy.

The application is a static website implemented in HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Radar content is defined entirely by JSON files in the `radars/` directory.

## Important files

- `README.md` — Project overview and hosting instructions.
- `radars/radars.json` — Registry of available radars.
- `radars/*.json` — Individual radar definitions.

## Retrieval

When answering questions about the radar:

1. Read `radars/radars.json`.
2. Determine the radar scope: use the requested radar, the `default` radar when none is specified, or every radar listed in the `radars` array when the question asks about all radars.
3. Load the JSON file for each radar in scope.
4. Resolve entry `quadrant` and `ring` indexes according to the Radar schema.
5. Present human-readable names according to the Radar schema.
6. Answer only from the radar data. Do not invent, infer, or summarise entries that are not present.

The radar JSON files are the authoritative source for all radar content.

## Radar schema

`radars/radars.json` contains:

- `default` — The id of the default radar to use when no radar is specified.
- `radars` — The list of available radars.
  - `id` — Internal identifier for locating a radar.
  - `label` — Human-readable radar name to present in answers.
  - `file` — Path to the radar JSON file.

Each radar contains:

- `title`
- `date`
- `caption`
- `quadrants` *(exactly four)*
  - `name` — Human-readable quadrant name to present in answers.
  - `purpose`
- `rings` *(exactly four)*
  - `name` — Human-readable ring name to present in answers.
  - `description`
- `entries` *(one or more)*
  - `label` — Human-readable entry name to present in answers.
  - `quadrant` — Zero-based index into the same radar's `quadrants` array.
  - `ring` — Zero-based index into the same radar's `rings` array.
  - `reason`
  - `moved` *(optional)* — Movement marker value. See Movement.
  - Any additional custom properties defined by the radar.

The application assumes every radar contains exactly four quadrants and four rings. Consumers should not expect these dimensions to vary.

Always resolve entry `quadrant` and `ring` indexes before presenting answers.

## Movement

`moved` controls the marker displayed on the radar.

| Value | Meaning |
|------:|---------|
| *(omitted)* or `0` | Unchanged or not specified |
| `1` | Moved in or increased confidence |
| `-1` | Moved out or reduced confidence |
| `2` | New or notable item |
